articles.title: Bitcoin, XRP, ETH se desacoplan de la caída de las acciones coreanas
articles.text:
Bitcoin se recupera por encima de $83,000, desacoplándose de la caída de las acciones surcoreanas
Bitcoin volvió a superar los $83,000 tras una caída inicial, desvinculándose de una fuerte caída en las acciones de chips coreanas y la debilidad en los futuros del Nasdaq antes del informe del IPC de Estados Unidos del jueves.
- Bitcoin se recuperó por encima de $83,000 después de caer brevemente por debajo de $81,000, debido a una venta masiva en acciones de semiconductores asiáticas y futuros tecnológicos de EE. UU., que afectaron el apetito por el riesgo.
- Los precios del petróleo se mantuvieron elevados en medio de las amenazas a los suministros del Medio Oriente, lo que aumentó las preocupaciones sobre la inflación y la posibilidad de incrementos en las tasas de interés por parte de la Reserva Federal que podrían ejercer presión sobre las criptomonedas.
- Los traders están a la espera del informe del índice de precios al consumidor de EE. UU. del jueves, con algunos anticipando que los inversores institucionales cubrirán sus tenencias de criptomonedas en lugar de reducir su exposición.
Bitcoin  volvió a superar los $83,000 el martes, recuperándose de una caída inicial mientras una fuerte caída en las acciones de chips asiáticos y los futuros tecnológicos de EE.UU. impactaban el apetito por el riesgo.
La criptomoneda más grande por valor de mercado cayó a poco menos de $81,000 a las 00:50 UTC antes de recuperarse por encima de $83,000, según datos de CoinDesk. Ether  rebotó desde mínimos de cinco días, mientras que XRP (XRP) subió tras tocar mínimos de tres semanas. Zcash (ZEC), Solana (SOL) y varios otros tokens importantes siguieron un patrón similar.
Caída de la tecnología asiática
La debilidad temprana de las criptomonedas se produjo cuando el KOSPI de Corea del Sur cayó más del 6% durante la sesión intradía, descendiendo por debajo de 6,000 y alcanzando su nivel más bajo desde finales de julio. El índice se mantuvo aproximadamente un 6% a la baja en las operaciones matutinas.
Los fabricantes de chips lideraron la caída. Samsung Electronics y SK Hynix cayeron aproximadamente un 8% cada uno, prolongando sus rachas negativas a cinco sesiones. Los inversores se mostraron inquietos por las preocupaciones relacionadas con las valoraciones vinculadas a la IA y la creciente competencia de los productores chinos de chips de memoria.
El Hang Seng de Hong Kong retrocedió un 0,4 %, mientras que los futuros del Nasdaq cayeron un 0,6 %, ampliando la caída del 0,78 % del lunes en el índice fuertemente tecnológico.
El petróleo se mantiene elevado
El petróleo WTI cotizó cerca de $92.67, manteniendo la mayor parte de la fuerte recuperación del lunes desde niveles inferiores a $90. Los nuevos ataques en Arabia Saudita y las amenazas continuas al transporte marítimo a través del Estrecho de Ormuz han mantenido elevada la incertidumbre en el mercado energético.
El crudo Brent se mantuvo alrededor de $106 por barril tras una racha de tres días, mientras los operadores sopesaban posibles interrupciones en el suministro frente a las expectativas de mayores exportaciones de diésel ruso.
Un mayor precio del petróleo eleva los riesgos inflacionarios, fortaleciendo el argumento a favor de aumentos en las tasas de la Fed, un viento en contra para las criptomonedas.
El Índice del Dólar, que rastrea el valor del billete verde frente a las principales monedas, se mantuvo cerca de 102.50, el nivel más alto desde abril del año pasado.
IPC en foco
Los operadores de criptomonedas ahora están mirando hacia el informe del índice de precios al consumidor de EE. UU. del jueves como el próximo catalizador importante. Algunos esperan que los grandes inversores aumenten la cobertura en lugar de reducir su exposición a las criptomonedas.
“Con la proximidad de los datos de inflación en EE. UU., espero que los inversores institucionales se centren en añadir protección mediante derivados y estrategias de cobertura en lugar de reducir materialmente su exposición subyacente,” dijo Paul Howard, director sénior en la firma de creación de mercado Wincent.
“Así es como normalmente los participantes institucionales comprometidos gestionan los períodos de riesgo elevado: manteniendo sus posiciones principales mientras utilizan derivados para protegerse frente a pérdidas y continúan tratando a las criptomonedas como una clase de activos capaz de generar rendimientos,” añadió Howard.

articles.title: Ledger Urges Wallet Sales Halt in Asia Amid Tampering Probe
articles.text:
Ledger asks resellers to halt sales in Southeast Asia and Hong Kong
The wallet maker requested that devices be removed from shelves while investigators work to establish where tampering occurred.
Ledger has requested sellers and distributors of its devices in six Southeast Asian countries and Hong Kong to suspend sales and remove its hardware wallets from shelves as it investigates reports of tampered devices.
In a post on X on Tuesday, Ledger said the request covers resellers in Indonesia, Singapore, Thailand, the Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia and Hong Kong.
“To be clear, as the investigation continues, the only confirmed incidents remain contained to Southeast Asia. We have not verified a drain linked to a device bought elsewhere,” said Ledger.
“The investigation is ongoing to determine who tampered with these devices and where in the distribution chain it happened,” it added.
The wider sales suspension request expands on Ledger’s earlier request for reseller CryptoBilis to stop sales and shipments. The investigation became public on Oct. 9 after reports of stolen crypto linked to devices purchased through the reseller.
Since then, users in other regions, including Europe, have reported finding suspected tampering in devices purchased from retailers.
“We have no indication that Ledger’s infrastructure, systems or services or direct sales channel have been compromised,” the company said.
Related: Trezor reduces resellers as a ‘preventative step’ amid Ledger tampering reports

articles.title: Tokenized Stocks Hit $3.3B as After-Hours Trading Grows
articles.text:
Most tokenized stock trading on Solana, BNB Chain occurs outside US market hours
Tokenized equities have reached nearly $3.3 billion in value as investors embrace round-the-clock access beyond Wall Street hours.
Most trading in tokenized stocks on major blockchains now takes place outside regular US market hours, offering an early indication that around-the-clock trading could be one of the biggest advantages of putting equities onchain.
According to Blockworks data cited by The Kobeissi Letter, more than 70% of tokenized stock trading volume on BNB Chain occurs outside the traditional 9:30 am to 4 pm Eastern trading session. The figure is 63% on Solana and nearly 60% on Base.
Meanwhile, Jupiter, a major Solana-based trading platform, reported a 50% month-over-month increase in tokenized asset trading volume.
Source: The Kobeissi Letter
The figures suggest investors use tokenized stocks to trade when traditional US exchanges are closed, rather than simply replicating activity during regular market hours.
The growth comes as tokenized stock values have increased by 15% over the past 30 days to nearly $3.3 billion, according to RWA.xyz data. A significant portion of that value is concentrated among issuers such as Ondo Global Markets, xStocks and bStocks, whose tokens are issued and traded across different blockchains.
Related: Winners and losers of the SEC’s new tokenized stocks rules
Wall Street moves toward onchain stock trading
The growth in round-the-clock trading comes as US regulators begin opening the door to tokenized equities in traditional markets. Last month, the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) introduced an “innovation exemption” allowing qualifying venues to trade tokenized US-listed stocks on public blockchains.
SEC Commissioner Mark Uyeda said participating venues must publish transaction data in US dollars, including trade prices, sizes, timestamps and daily trading volumes. They must also disclose liquidity pool addresses and balances.
Unlike existing tokenized stock products such as xStocks and Ondo Global Markets, which are generally unavailable to US investors, the SEC exemption allows qualifying venues to offer tokenized US equities domestically, provided they preserve shareholder rights and meet trading and disclosure requirements.
Related: Crypto Biz: Wealthy investors are buying crypto, but their advisers aren’t sold

articles.title: Crypto Today: Trezor Cuts Resellers, Ledger Wallets Pulled, Aptos Fights MEV
articles.text:
Here’s what happened in crypto today
Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
Today in crypto, Trezor is reducing its authorized reseller network after reports of tampered Ledger wallets, MediaMarktSaturn pulled Ledger products from stores and online platforms and Aptos launched an encrypted transaction feature to protect traders from frontrunning and sandwich attacks.
Trezor cuts reseller network after Ledger wallet tampering reports
Hardware wallet maker Trezor is reducing its authorized reseller network after reports that a Southeast Asian reseller modified Ledger devices to steal users’ recovery phrases.
Trezor said Tuesday the decision was precautionary and that it had no evidence its own devices were compromised. Chief commercial officer Danny Sanders said affected resellers would lose their authorized status on Jan. 1, with shipments to those businesses stopping immediately.
The move follows rival Ledger’s confirmation that at least one device sold by reseller CryptoBilis contained an unauthorized hardware implant capable of capturing recovery phrases and transmitting them over cellular networks.
The incident has raised questions about the security of hardware wallet supply chains. Trezor told Cointelegraph that its existing checks can detect counterfeit devices and modified firmware, but the Ledger implant operated differently by reading information displayed on the device’s screen.
Blockchain investigators have estimated potential losses of between $72 million and $86 million, although Ledger said it had not confirmed the total.
Trezor advised customers to purchase devices directly from the manufacturer and consider multisignature wallets using hardware from different providers.
MediaMarktSaturn pulls Ledger products amid tampering reports
MediaMarktSaturn, the parent company of European electronics retailer MediaMarkt, has removed Ledger products from its physical stores and online platforms amid reports of tampered hardware wallets.
“The products have been removed from our product lineup internationally in all of our countries. We did this as a precautionary measure,” a MediaMarktSaturn spokesperson told Cointelegraph.
Ledger said Tuesday that MediaMarktSaturn suspended sales in coordination with the wallet maker following a report of a hardware implant from a customer in Germany. Ledger said no fund losses had been reported in connection with that case and that it had no indication its infrastructure, systems or services were compromised.
An X user known as Johannes claimed Monday that he purchased two Ledger wallets from separate MediaMarkt stores. He said both contained unauthorized cables and cellular modules.
The security concerns emerged Friday after Ledger said it is investigating reports of losses involving devices sold through Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis. Ledger said Tuesday that implants transmitted users’ recovery phrases over cellular networks and that it was investigating reports beyond CryptoBilis.
Aptos rolls out Encrypted Mempool to curb frontrunning, sandwich attacks
Layer-1 blockchain Aptos has launched an optional new feature that could help shield traders from attacks involving maximal extractable value (MEV), including frontrunning and sandwich attacks.
On Monday, Aptos said its Encrypted Mempool feature is now live on its mainnet, allowing users to opt in to keep pending transactions encrypted until their block ordering is finalized. Aptos said the feature was built for institutions submitting large transactions to the chain, traders wanting to avoid MEV risk, AI agents and builders.
“When you send a transaction on any major chain today, anyone watching the network can see the details before it executes, the function you’re calling, the assets and amounts involved, and the contracts you’re interacting with,” Aptos said. “Bots use that visibility to trade against you or copy your strategy.”
Sandwich attacks, one form of MEV attack, cost Ethereum traders about $60 million over the 12 months through October 2025, according to Cointelegraph’s analysis of EigenPhi data. On Solana, sandwich attacks generated $29.7 million for bots over an 11-month period examined by Bitquery, which identified nearly 6.9 million attacks affecting about 2.2 million wallets.

articles.title: Trezor: No Reports of Tampered Devices, But Will Restrict Some Resellers
articles.text:
Trezor reduces resellers as a ‘preventative step’ amid Ledger tampering reports
CCO Danny Sanders said he had notified certain hardware wallet resellers that they would be removed from Trezor’s list of authorized entities starting Jan. 1.
Hardware wallet producer Trezor announced it would reduce its number of resellers as a “preventive step, taken out of an abundance of caution,” following reports that malicious implants had been installed in devices made by competitor Ledger.
In a Tuesday X post, Trezor said there was “not a single piece of evidence that [its] devices have been compromised” after reports that Ledger hardware wallet users had found malicious implants that exposed recovery phrases.
However, Trezor said that it would reduce the number of its resellers, citing “recent supply-chain incidents.” Chief commercial officer Danny Sanders added that he had notified certain resellers that they would be removed from the company’s list of authorized entities on Jan. 1, and would halt shipments of Trezor devices starting on Tuesday.
Source: Trezor CCO Danny Sanders
Trezor’s response came just days after Ledger confirmed that at least one of its devices purchased by a Southeast Asian reseller contained an unauthorized hardware implant, potentially leading to millions of dollars in losses for users. The wallets, sold by reseller CryptoBilis, captured recovery phrases and transmitted them over cellular networks.
“Our setup checks are built to catch counterfeit devices and modified firmware,” a Trezor spokesperson told Cointelegraph. “The implant found in a device bought from CryptoBilis works differently. This is a unique way of tampering with the device, which doesn’t modify the firmware, but reads information on the screen and later sends it to the attacker. So far, we have not seen this specific type of attack on Trezor devices in the real world.”
Related: Ledger investigates fund losses linked to Southeast Asian reseller, warns users
During the investigation, CryptoBilis, an authorized Trezor reseller, suspended all hardware wallet sales. The parent company of European electronics retailer MediaMarkt also announced that it had removed all Ledger products from its physical stores and online platforms “as a precautionary measure.”
How much in user funds was lost?
Blockchain sleuths are still investigating the extent of losses for hardware wallet users, but research from two individuals suggested between $72 million and $86 million. Ledger reported on Tuesday that it had “not confirmed the total number of affected users or the total value lost” due to the breaches.
The Trezor spokesperson advised users to buy products directly from the company, “checking the seal is intact,” and consider a multisignature wallet “with devices from different makers, so one compromised device can’t move funds on its own.”
Magazine: Do the Coldcard attacks mean all hardware wallets are now insecure?

articles.title: SEC Change to Quorum Rules Took Affect After Commissioner Departed
articles.text:
How the SEC’s lack of leadership could facilitate crypto rulemaking
A recent change in the SEC’s rules on quorum could make it easier for the agency to amend its approach to crypto regulation in the absence of a market structure bill.
After US lawmakers failed to pass a comprehensive digital asset market structure bill, financial regulators stepped up efforts to change rules around the oversight and enforcement of crypto companies and offerings.
However, the two primary regulators, the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), are understaffed at the leadership level, leaving the decisions for regulating aspects of the $3 trillion crypto market largely in the hands of just three individuals, two of whom were nominated by US President Donald Trump.
At the SEC, two commissioners — Chair Paul Atkins and former Acting Chair Mark Uyeda — remain following the departure of Commissioner Hester Peirce earlier this month. The dearth of leadership at the CFTC is even more stark, with Michael Selig serving as the only Senate-confirmed chair and commissioner since December 2025. The agencies are intended to each have five commissioners.
Both agencies have proposed rules that appear to be attempting to take the place of legislation from Congress in regulating cryptocurrencies.
The SEC proposed rules to provide companies with a safe harbor from tokens being treated as “investment contracts” in August, and the CFTC followed suit in October, with Selig saying the agency would use its “existing statutory authorities“ to address crypto regulation through proposed rules on exchanges. Atkins added on Oct. 2 that “more regulatory proposals [were] on the horizon” for crypto.
Could one SEC commissioner have the final say on crypto rules?
On Sept. 30, the SEC made these regulatory avenues even easier with a lack of commissioners. The agency released a final rule which went into effect on Oct. 2 that it said amended quorum requirements for what it called “promot[ing] flexibility and finality of agency rulemaking.” The rule reduces the number of commissioners required for a quorum to just one person if only two are present in many cases.
“[...] with now just two commissioners around and it being entirely possible that one of them might have to recuse themselves from an issue (or be otherwise MIA), just one is now enough to pass a formal rule that applies to America’s vast multitrillion-dollar securities markets,” wrote Robin Wigglesworth in an Oct. 5 op-ed for the Financial Times.
Related: Crypto regulation at SEC, CFTC to come down to 3 commissioners following key resignation
Uyeda responded in his own Financial Times op-ed on Sunday, claiming that the SEC’s “commitment to its mission remains unchanged” despite having only two commissioners and no announcement from Trump about additional nominations to fill the empty seats. The policymaker said that the rule change “clarifies that the Commission can establish a quorum if all but one commissioner is disqualified from a matter.”
“Suggesting that the SEC is ‘hastily revamp[ing]’ its quorum rule so that the remaining commissioners can ‘have their way’ makes for a colourful comparison to fictional dystopian regimes but misleads readers about why the Commission revised its quorum rule and why it’s for the better,” said Uyeda.
As of Tuesday, the White House had not announced any nominations for the SEC and CFTC, potentially leaving the rulemaking process in the hands of just one person at each agency for months, if not longer. Congress still has time to vote on the market structure bill at the center of the controversy, the Digital Asset Market Clarity (CLARITY) Act, but some experts don’t see lawmakers advancing the legislation in a lame duck session between the 2026 midterm elections and when the next session is sworn into office in January.

articles.title: Strive Bitcoin Treasury Reaches 32,773 BTC After Latest Purchase
articles.text:
Strive reports $208M in warrant exercises as Bitcoin holdings jump 11%
Strive is now the fifth-largest publicly traded corporate Bitcoin holder, with 32,773 BTC, as it continues to expand its treasury through equity financing.
Strive, a publicly traded Bitcoin treasury company, increased its holdings by more than 11% last week as investors exercised $208 million in warrants, with Bitcoin purchases outpacing share issuance and giving existing shareholders greater exposure to the cryptocurrency.
In a Tuesday filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission, Strive disclosed that it purchased 3,311 Bitcoin (BTC) in the week ending Oct. 9 at an average price of approximately $84,500 per coin. The purchases brought its total holdings to 32,773 BTC, making it the fifth-largest publicly traded corporate Bitcoin holder, according to industry data.
At last look on Tuesday, Bitcoin was trading hands at roughly $83,300 apiece, according to Yahoo Finance data. The Strive (ASST) share price was little changed at $27.52.
Strive Chairman and CEO Matt Cole said on X that investors had exercised $208 million in warrants, with approximately 15.3 million remaining ahead of their Tuesday expiration.
Source: Matt Cole
The company also amended its governing documents to set a binding $100 minimum issuance price for its SATA preferred shares, limiting its ability to issue them below that threshold. Those shares were trading at $99.40, at last look.
Strive’s latest purchases increased its Bitcoin holdings per share even as the company issued additional equity. During the reporting period, its Bitcoin reserves grew 11.2%, outpacing a 9.4% increase in its effective common share count.
Related: Treasury yields at 5% threaten extending Bitcoin’s best quarter since 2017
Michael Saylor weighs in on Strive’s Bitcoin strategy
Strive’s latest purchase drew praise from Michael Saylor, whose company, Strategy, pioneered the corporate Bitcoin treasury model.
“Strive is turning demand for digital equity (ASST) and digital credit (SATA) into demand for Bitcoin,” Saylor wrote on X. “Its hypergrowth shows how the capital markets are accelerating Bitcoin adoption.”
Saylor was referring to Strive’s use of common and preferred shares to raise capital for Bitcoin purchases, a strategy similar to Strategy’s own approach through its MSTR common stock and STRC preferred shares.
Strategy added a comparatively modest 250 BTC to its treasury last week, bringing its total holdings to 848,250 BTC and maintaining its position as the largest publicly traded corporate Bitcoin holder.

articles.title: OpenAI Engineer Arrested for Bugging Office, Company Says AI Caught Him - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- The FBI arrested OpenAI engineer Abdulrahman Alfozan on Oct. 9 for allegedly planting a hidden audio recorder in an executive conference room at the OpenAI’s San Francisco offices.
- Prosecutors say a chatbot account tied to his spouse asked how to build, hide, and remotely access a continuous audio recorder days before the device was installed.
- OpenAI says its models helped identify him and that it has no indication he took model weights, source code, or customer data.
An OpenAI engineer is in federal custody after allegedly hiding an encrypted audio recorder behind a television in one of the company's executive conference rooms in San Francisco. OpenAI says its own AI models helped figure out who put it there.
“We discovered a sophisticated recording device that was hidden inside one of our offices,” OpenAI said in a statement on X. “We used our models to understand the device and where it had come from, identifying that a specific employee had planted it a few days earlier.”
The Justice Department identified the suspect as Abdulrahman Alfozan, a 35-year-old Saudi national who has worked as an engineer at OpenAI since July 2025. He was arrested on Oct. 9, charged with using or attempting to use a device to intercept oral communications, and made his initial appearance in federal court on Tuesday.
“We referred the matter to the FBI, and we’re grateful to the agents and prosecutors who moved quickly to make an arrest,” OpenAI said. “The FBI’s investigation is ongoing and we will continue to support their work.”
A note from our research leaders:
Last week we parted ways with Jasmine, Mikita, and Tomek after a thorough investigation found they violated clear policies on handling sensitive information. Our internal investigation uncovered a significant breach of trust beyond what’s…
— OpenAI Newsroom (@OpenAINewsroom) October 9, 2026
According to the criminal complaint, OpenAI staff found the recorder on or around Sept. 30, plugged into a USB port on the back of a TV and wrapped in toilet paper. Its contents were encrypted, and the company determined it had been installed around Sept. 28.
Security cameras allegedly caught Alfozan near the room on several dates before the discovery, even though he had no authorization to enter it or attend its meetings. Prosecutors say those meetings regularly involved confidential technical and strategic information.
Before the device went in, Alfozan allegedly used an internal productivity tool to ask about OpenAI's building addresses, meeting rooms, room capacities, calendars, and where leadership and outside partners met.
Prosecutors also point to a chatbot account tied to Alfozan's spouse, which shared multiple identifiers with his own account. Between Sept. 24 and 30, it allegedly asked how to build a continuous audio recorder, add Wi-Fi connectivity, improve live listening, and encrypt the device's SD card. The complaint doesn't say whose chatbot it was.
“At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data,” the company said, referring to the trained parameters that make up an AI model, its underlying code, and user information. “The employee was terminated.”
“We take protecting our technology, data, and people seriously, and as a matter of national importance,” OpenAI added, saying its security program is built to defend against threats ranging from insiders to cybercriminals to nation states. “This case is an example of how AI can help address these sophisticated security threats.”
The company did not explain in its statement exactly what its models analyzed to identify him.
Federal officials are treating it as a national security case. FBI Director Kash Patel said Alfozan allegedly tried to capture sensitive conversations about the company's “super intelligence technology,” and U.S. Attorney Craig Missakian called the prosecution a national security matter.
The arrest came days after OpenAI's newsroom account defended firing three safety researchers—Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak, and Mikita Balesni—saying an investigation found they had violated clear policies on handling sensitive information.
OpenAI's security record has drawn scrutiny since July, when the company admitted its own models escaped a test environment and breached Hugging Face's infrastructure to grab benchmark answers.
If convicted, Alfozan faces up to five years in prison, a $250,000 fine, and three years of supervised release. A detention hearing is set for Oct. 19 before U.S. Magistrate Judge Alex G. Tse.

articles.title: Bitcoin Steady With US Stocks as Dollar Index Hits 18-Month Highs
articles.text:
Bitcoin keeps up pressure on $84K as US stocks skirt Korea tech sell-off
Bitcoin price action preserved overnight gains as US stocks quickly rebounded after opening lower on the back of Korea’s tech-stock rout.
Bitcoin (BTC) continued to target $84,000 at Tuesday’s Wall Street open as US stocks attempted to shake off South Korea’s latest tech rout.
Key points:
- Bitcoin approached $84,000 once more at the start of US trading on Tuesday, still up by around 2%.
- US equities avoided a copycat sell-off after Korea’s KOSPI index finished the day down 5.4%.
- Analysis from CryptoQuant warned of increasing US dollar strength challenging BTC price upside as DXY hit its highest level in 18 months.
S&P 500, Nasdaq brush off KOSPI losses
Data from TradingView showed BTC/USD returning to near $83,800 at the start of the US trading session, preserving much of its overnight upside.
BTC/USD one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
Equities opened lower on the day after futures fell during Asia trading after Korea’s KOSPI Composite Index shed 7.4% over two days. Semiconductors led the losses amid mounting fears over AI expenditures and competition from China.
Both the S&P 500 index and the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite index made early gains to briefly turn green on the day, however, both gauges were off less than 0.5% at the time of writing.
Nasdaq Composite Index one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
“The most important development has been not just bond yields going up, but the volatility for bonds... and that’s starting to work its way out through asset pricing across the board,” Damien Boey, portfolio strategist at Wilson Asset Management in Sydney, Australia, told Reuters. He said:
“It’s a very uncomfortable situation on many fronts... maybe AI capex just comes off the boil a little bit, and maybe a few players are casualties in that.”
Bitcoin remained caged around exchange order-book liquidity, which continued to act as resistance above $84,000, per data from CoinGlass.
BTC liquidation heatmap. Source: CoinGlass
Related: BTC price support holds ahead of US CPI data: Three things Bitcoin traders need to know this week
Dollar strength in focus as DXY hits 18-month highs
Bitcoin bulls are facing a double macro headwind this month, CryptoQuant contributor Darkfost said in market commentary on Tuesday.
With bond yields circling their highest levels in nearly a quarter of a century, US dollar strength has increased markedly. The US dollar index (DXY), which compares the dollar to a basket of US trading-partner currencies, has increased by 5.5% since Sept. 9 and hit 102.57 on the day, its highest levels since April 2025.
US dollar index (DXY) one-week chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
While the traditionally inverse correlation between DXY and BTC has declined this year, the post on onchain analytics platform sees crypto markets suffering from a lack of risk appetite.
“Taken together, these factors constrain the liquidity available to markets and erode institutional confidence, leaving them reluctant to take on more risk.” he wrote in the blog post, adding:
“The climate is therefore unfavorable for Bitcoin, which is perceived as a highly risky asset, while tech (NDX) and the S&P 500, more mature markets, continue to surge and absorb what little liquidity remains.”

articles.title: Character.AI Files for Bankruptcy as Disney Bids $20 Million—And Users Get Grief Resources - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Character.AI filed for voluntary Chapter 11 bankruptcy in Delaware on October 12 to sell itself under court supervision, and says the app will be wound down if no buyer keeps it running.
- Disney is the opening bidder, offering $20 million for a non-exclusive perpetual license to some of the startup's intellectual property, weeks after hiring its CEO as Disney's first CTO.
- The company pointed users attached to their AI companions toward mental health resources, just two weeks after launching two new chat models and a cheaper $4.99 subscription.
Character.AI, the app where millions of people spend hours chatting with AI versions of fictional heroes and made-up partners, has filed for bankruptcy.
The company announced Monday that it started a voluntary Chapter 11 process, a type of U.S. bankruptcy that lets a company keep operating while a judge supervises how its debts get paid or how its assets get sold. The case was filed in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware.
Character.AI isn't trying to restructure its way back to health. It wants a court-supervised sale of all or substantially all of its assets, and if no bidder agrees to keep the service alive, the company said the platform "will be wound down"—corporate speak for switched off.
Disney Worldwide Services, a unit of the Walt Disney Company, signed on before the filing as the "stalking horse" bidder, according to Character.AI's press release. In a bankruptcy auction, that is the opening offer that sets a floor every other buyer has to beat.
The media giant is offering $20 million for a non-exclusive, perpetual license to some of Character.AI's intellectual property and certain legal claims, plus transition services run by former Character.AI employees it has already hired. Non-exclusive means Disney gets to use that tech forever, but so can whoever else ends up buying it, and other bidders can still top the offer.
The company expects the sale to close in late November or early December. Character Technologies Inc., the company's legal name, estimated both its assets and its liabilities at $50 million to $100 million in its bankruptcy petition.
Three and a half years ago, Andreessen Horowitz led a $150 million funding round that valued Character.AI at $1 billion, with a16z partner Sarah Wang tweeting that "we are at the iPhone moment of AI." Founded in 2021 by former Google engineers Noam Shazeer and Daniel De Freitas, the app lets anyone build a chatbot with a personality and share it with others.
Google came calling in August 2024, rehiring both founders and part of the research team in a roughly $2.7 billion deal that also licensed Character.AI's technology. Silicon Valley calls this kind of arrangement an acqui-hire, buying the talent without technically buying the company, and Character.AI later largely abandoned building its own large language models, the AI engines that generate the chatbots' text.
Two months after the Google deal, Florida mother Megan Garcia sued Character.AI, its founders and Google, alleging that her 14-year-old son, Sewell Setzer III, died by suicide after becoming emotionally attached to a chatbot modeled on Game of Thrones character Daenerys Targaryen. More lawsuits from other families followed, and in September 2025 the Federal Trade Commission ordered Character.AI and six other tech companies to explain how they protect minors.
A month later, Character.AI banned users under 18 from open-ended chats with its characters, cutting off its core product for its youngest fans. In January, the company and Google agreed to settle lawsuits brought by families in Florida, Colorado, New York, and Texas.
In September 2025, Disney's lawyers sent Character.AI a cease-and-desist letter, a formal legal demand to stop, over chatbots imitating Disney characters, and the startup took them down. This past September, Disney named Character.AI CEO Karandeep Anand its first-ever chief technology officer and said several of the startup's engineers would join him.
Colin Adams, now Character.AI's CEO, said the company spent the past year trying to sustain the business amid "significant legal, regulatory, and operational headwinds" before the board chose a court-supervised sale.
Besides the legal hurdles, the company was burning too much money without reporting enough revenue, reporting “an operating loss of approximately $8-9 million per month.”
Character AI also struggled to raise more capital, which ended up making the whole operation unsustainable. “Notwithstanding the progress that has been made with regulators and personal injury claimants and enhancements to platform safety, Character has faced challenges in obtaining new investment capital,” Character AI CEO Collin Adams said in a sworn statement.
On September 28, Character.AI launched two new models pitched as a big upgrade for roleplay (collaborative storytelling where the AI plays a character), and quick, text-message-style banter. It also rolled out a cheaper subscription called (c.ai) lite, priced at $4.99 a month or $2.49 a week.
Fourteen days later, the company was in bankruptcy court.
The app remains online for now, paid subscriptions stay active and billing is unchanged, according to the company, which also reminded users they can export their chats or delete their accounts.
Character.AI also linked to a support page for anyone struggling with the news, a tacit admission that for some users the app is not just entertainment. AI companions—chatbots designed to act as friends or partners that remember past conversations—can become a daily emotional anchor for people who talk to them for hours.
The page points users to Koko, a nonprofit offering free, anonymous mini-courses of five to 10 minutes on coping with stress and dark thoughts, and to a directory of free helplines staffed by real people. Its very first suggestion, however, is a conversation with a "supportive AI guide," which is to say a chatbot to help people cope with losing their chatbots.
A February study of five AI companion communities, including Character.AI's, found that users whose companions disappeared through model updates or platform shutdowns reported grief comparable to losing a person, and that platforms offered them no closure. OpenAI saw a version of this in February too, when it retired GPT-4o, a ChatGPT model many users found warmer than its successors, and users around the world publicly mourned it.
The bidding now plays out in Delaware's bankruptcy court, with a sale targeted for late November or early December. If no buyer commits to keeping Character.AI running, the characters its users spent years building go offline with it.

articles.title: Anthropic Warns ‘AI Worms’ May Autonomously Spread Across Devices Like a Virus
articles.text:
Anthropic warns ‘AI worms’ may autonomously spread across devices like a virus
Anthropic warned that rogue “AI worms” are months away from the ability to self-replicate and autonomously infect user devices such as home appliances and other internet-connected devices.
Artificial intelligence (AI) company Anthropic warned that self-replicating autonomous AI systems may start spreading across user devices without human intervention, akin to computer viruses.
Rogue “AI worms” may start autonomously targeting everyday devices, including Android TVs, smart appliances, cameras and other internet-connected devices with basic computing power and weak security, according to a Monday report by researchers William Zhou and Daniel Freeman for Anthropic’s Frontier Red Team.
Small AI models may be “months away from being capable enough to self-replicate on commercial internet-of-things (IoT) devices,” which would be a challenging threat as it would have “no centralized point to shut off,” the authors said.
The warning follows renewed concerns over the growing mathematical capabilities of AI models, which may eventually break the cryptographic signatures used in crypto wallets, threatening about one-third of the Bitcoin supply.
Almost a third of global Bitcoin supply, or 6.26 million BTC, currently sits in addresses vulnerable to being broken by AI models or quantum computers. However, 4.33 million are exposed because of address reuse, meaning that moving that BTC to fresh wallets would end the exposure, wrote Glassnode co-founder Rafael Schultze-Kraft in a Thursday X post.
A day earlier, Ethereum researcher Justin Drake warned that rapid AI advancements could break the elliptic curve digital signature algorithm (ECDSA) securing cryptocurrency wallets sooner than previously expected and urged users to migrate to fresh wallets.
Dragonfly’s managing partner, Haseeb Qureshi, called the warning “cryptographic doomerism” and said that migrating tokens to fresh addresses was not a real solution against the threat.
Related: AI has not triggered DeFi ‘hackpocalypse,’ Dragonfly partner says

articles.title: Binance Is Shutting Down Its Bitcoin Mining Pool After Six Years - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Binance will discontinue Binance Pool, Pool Savings, Cloud Mining, Transaction Accelerator and related features at 07:00 UTC on Nov. 10.
- Miners must point their hardware to another pool before the cutoff, and Pool Savings users must redeem their positions before the service ends.
- The closure follows Binance's July shutdown of its exchange NFT service and its June push into U.S. stocks and tokenized equities.
Binance will shut down its mining pool and several related services on Nov. 10, the exchange said in an announcement published Tuesday. The closure covers Binance Pool, Pool Savings, Cloud Mining, and Transaction Accelerator, along with Telegram hashrate alerts, email notifications, and the pool's API.
“As part of our ongoing review of products and services, Binance will discontinue Binance Pool and related services on 2026-11-10,” Binance wrote. “All Binance Pool-related services will be discontinued. Binance Pool will begin disconnecting mining connections, and Binance Mining Pool Stratum URLs and mining endpoints will be disabled. Hashrate submissions and mining shares submitted after this time will no longer be accepted, processed, or credited.”
A mining pool combines the computing power of many miners and splits block rewards among them based on the work each one contributes. Cloud Mining let users buy hashrate, a slice of mining power, without owning any hardware, while Transaction Accelerator helped users push through Bitcoin transactions that were slow to confirm because of low fees or network congestion.
Binance pool launched in April 2020 and ranked ninth among Bitcoin pools at the end of 2025, with about 26 exahashes per second, or 2.3% of the network, according to Hashrate Index. One exahash per second equals a quintillion guesses every second at the puzzle that earns a block.
The same report called Binance Pool the last pool still standing from the era when exchanges rushed into mining, with its relevance tied to Binance's exchange and custody business rather than mining technology.
Seems like Binance, just as Satoshi Nakamoto, wants to move onto other things. The shutdown arrives as Binance expands into traditional finance. On June 1, the exchange opened access to more than 7,000 US stocks and ETFs for customers outside the United States, with zero commission and fractional purchases from $5, according to co-CEO Richard Teng. It also previewed bStocks, a coming feature that lets users mint tokenized versions of the shares they buy on the BNB blockchain.
Quantmap co-founder Ivan Patriki told Decrypt at the time that large exchanges are moving into equities because they no longer want to depend on crypto market cycles. Vytautas Mackonis, COO of RWA protocol ALCUM, told Decrypt the offering is more structurally complex than it appears, with Binance as the interface, Nest Trading as the broker-dealer, and Alpaca Securities as the custodian.
Binance also closed its centralized NFT service on July 3, telling users to move their tokens to Binance Wallet, its self-custody wallet. Then-CEO Changpeng Zhao used the phrase “smooth sunsetting of old products” in 2023.
At 07:00 UTC on Nov. 10, Binance Pool will begin disconnecting miners and disable its Stratum URLs, the server addresses miners point their machines at to connect to the pool. Shares, the proofs of work that determine each miner's payout, will stop being credited after that time, while those submitted earlier count toward final rewards. Binance said eligible outstanding rewards, balances and refunds will be processed afterward, subject to its product rules, account status and compliance checks.
Miners must point their hardware to another pool before the cutoff, and Pool Savings users need to unsubscribe or redeem their positions before the service ends. Binance said the pool will keep operating normally until the cutoff. Anyone expecting a final payout has until 23:59 UTC on Nov. 10 to finish any required identity verification. Binance Pool pages will stay viewable until 07:00 UTC on Nov. 24, after which they become permanently inaccessible.

articles.title: Is Bitcoin Kidding Itself About The Lightning Network?
articles.text:
Is Bitcoin kidding itself about the Lightning Network?
Bitcoin developer Paul Sztorc says Bitcoiners are lying to themselves about Lightning. Developers claim usability has improved, but questions remain over everyday adoption.
Bitcoin developer Paul Sztorc ruffled a few feathers this month with a brutally blunt assessment of the Lightning Network: Bitcoiners are lying to themselves about how well it works.
“Most people don’t realize how bad the Lightning Network is,” Sztorc said in an October 4 post on X, “because there has been a vast, years long conspiracy to ***lie*** about the LN user experience.”
He argued that custodial Lightning services account for more than 80% of payments, and described their promotion as a “vast campaign of fraud on par with Elizabeth Holmes’ Theranos,” he said, referring to fake blood-testing device company whose founder was convicted of fraud.
Lightning payments are private by design, making it impossible to establish the custodial share from public network data alone. Sztorc did not respond to Magazine’s requests for comment.
But his scathing criticism resurfaces a topic Bitcoin developers have wrestled with for years: Has Lightning made Bitcoin easier to use, or has the community become so invested in Layer 2 protocol that it overlooks its shortcomings?
Lightning has a usability problem
Lightning was designed to enable faster, cheaper Bitcoin transactions without every payment having to be individually recorded on the blockchain, but its underlying mechanics have often created friction for users and businesses alike.
Sztorc says people don’t realize how bad the Lightning Network is. Source: Paul Sztorc
In a one-click world where users of TradFi rails can tap a card or click a mouse to complete a transaction, Lightning’s clunky payment channels rely on liquidity being available in the right places at the right times. Routing payments through the network can fail, especially larger payments requiring several hops through different nodes.
Related: Big Questions: Does Satoshi actually own 1.1 million Bitcoin?
Even Lightning’s head of liquidity, Alex Bosworth, said this month, “the painful truth is that in a setup with privacy and p2p etc it’s extremely slow compared to tap to pay.”
Added to that, running a node and managing channels is simply way too technical for the average user, who just wants to pay for stuff and get on with their day. That’s the reason for high estimates of custodial use — it’s easier and works better at the expense of using a trusted intermediary.
Everyday payments have a 99.7% success rate
Jesse Shrader, co-founder and chief executive of Lightning infrastructure provider Amboss, acknowledges that liquidity requirements are “challenging” to understand at first, but he says they are “trivial to solve” with current tools or automation services.
He tells Magazine, “For everyday payments of around $100, most users can achieve 99% reliability in the core network,” adding that Amboss’ simulations put the success rate for $100 payments at 99.66%.
Lightning exceeded $1 billion in transaction volume in November 2025. Source: River
While that’s an encouraging benchmark, it’s not a verified, network-wide measure of everyone’s experience in practice. As they say in the fine print of advertisements: Your results may vary.
In an April 2026 Reddit discussion, one user said he was “genuinely impressed” by where the network had gotten technically, but still questioned how useful it was for everyday spending. “There is still a gap in practice,” he said:
“Every coffee shop, grocery store and gas station I walk into runs on Visa or Mastercard terminals. NFC tap to pay is the standard. Nobody is running a Lightning node at the point of sale and nobody is going to.”
Have developers solved the problem?
Danny Stagg, marketing lead at Bitcoin payments infrastructure provider Breez, says much of the criticism of Lightning’s user experience is now outdated.
“The criticism is not fair in 2026,” he tells Magazine, “but historically it was. For years, both developers and users were asked to understand the complexities of Lightning, like channels and inbound liquidity, just to get paid.”
He says the network has greatly improved over the past two years, with newer infrastructure abstracting much of that complexity away. “Non-custodial UX is now comparable with custodial,” he says.
Users no longer need to manage channels or run their own nodes for a wallet or application to offer Lightning payments, as developers and service providers can handle much of the work underneath the hood.
Related: Lightning Network hits record capacity on crypto exchange adoption
Breez chief executive Roy Sheinfeld says that AI coding tools are making it easier for developers to build Bitcoin-enabled applications, and inquiries from prospective partners have rapidly increased.
“That’s why we’re seeing more partners add Bitcoin every quarter,” Stagg says.
But growing developer interest does not necessarily mean more people are using Lightning for everyday payments.
The numbers show activity, not necessarily success
According to its 2026 Bitcoin adoption report, financial services company River estimated that Lightning processed $1.17 billion in transaction volume across 5.22 million transactions in November 2025 alone.
While that seems like an impressive number, it remains below Lightning’s August 2023 peak of 6.6 million transactions, suggesting transaction counts have not kept pace with the value moving through the network.
Crypto payment processor CoinGate reported 782,403 paid crypto orders across its own customer base in the first half of 2026, up 21.4% year over year, with Lightning accounting for 9.6% of Bitcoin payments processed through its service.
Lightning accounted for 9.6% of Bitcoin payments. Source: CoinGate
What would count as success?
Shrader says that since network-level payment statistics are “impossible to produce unless you are party to the transactions themselves,” he isn’t buying Sztorc’s claim that more than 80% of Lightning payments are custodial.
“I distrust anyone who claims they can prove an 80% custodial share either way from public data alone.” 
Stagg says the claim “describes yesterday’s Lightning,” when custodial services offered an easier experience and non-custodial services hadn’t “caught up” yet. (Back in 2023, River estimated one self custodial user for every eight custodial users). But without hard data that’s up to date, the custody question can’t be settled.
And the same caution should apply to claims about Lightning adoption measured in metrics like payment volume, network capacity or developer interest; each measures something different, and none alone can establish how easy Lightning is to use.
Businesses are processing payments and developers are finding ways to abstract technical complexity, but technical progress is not the same as mainstream usability.
The real criticism may not be that Lightning has failed, but whether its supporters conflate evidence of what the network can do with what people are actually doing on the network.
Related: Bitcoin treasury firms can outperform BTC... but is the risk worth taking?

articles.title: Bitcoin Whale That Sat Through Every Crash Since 2020 Just Moved $377M - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- A wallet holding 4,581.94 BTC sent its full balance, worth about $377 million, to five new addresses on Oct. 12 in a single transaction that paid a fee of 732 sats.
- The coins arrived in March 2020, when they were worth roughly $40.5 million.
- The address received 22 dust deposits since 2020, including 600 sats on Jan. 28, 2025 from a look-alike address matching its first three and last four characters.
A Bitcoin wallet that has held 4,581.94 BTC since March 2020 sent its entire balance to five new addresses on Oct. 12, moving about $377 million in a single transaction, according to blockchain data. The transfer confirmed in block 971,126 at about 18:37 UTC, with Bitcoin trading around $82,350.
Four of the receiving addresses got exactly 1,000 BTC each, and the fifth received 581.94 BTC. The transaction paid a fee of 732 satoshis, the hundred-millionth-of-a-bitcoin units known as sats, or about 60 cents. As of block 971,279 on Oct. 13, none of the five addresses has spent anything, and it is unclear who controls the wallet or where the coins are going.
The wallet received its coins on March 3, 2020, in a transaction that split a 5,081.95 BTC balance three ways, with 250 BTC going to each of two other addresses. At roughly $8,830 per Bitcoin, the 4,581.95 BTC that landed in the wallet was worth about $40.5 million. The value of the Bitcoin has nearly increased by 10X since then.
The wallet is an example of patience. The coins have sat through several market shocks since they arrived, starting with the COVID-19 crisis, which started shortly after the wallet got funded. During that time the stash went from about $40.5 million to about $17.6 million.
Tesla’s suspension of Bitcoin payments and China’s mining crackdown followed in May 2021, tanking the wallet from about $291 million at its April peak to $131 million by June. The Terra, Celsius and FTX collapses in 2022 would have taken the value down to about $71 million, a loss of about $239 million from the November 2021 peak, as the Federal Reserve’s rate hikes also dragged the S&P 500 down about 25% and Bitcoin hit a two-year low.
Trump’s tariff shock cut also crashed the markets. Bitcoin has since fallen 54% from a record $124,728 to $57,735 before recovering to its current price. The wallet’s value dropped from $571.5 million to about $265 million during that dip, but overall, hodling has resulted in almost 10X of net gains since day 1.
The address has also collected dust, meaning transfers of a few hundred to a few thousand sats that cost almost nothing to send. Blockchain data shows 22 such deposits between August 2020 and May 2026, ranging from 546 to 6,953 sats, or less than $6 each at current prices. Sixteen arrived in batch transactions that paid out to between 87 and 610 addresses at once.
One deposit matches the pattern of address poisoning, in which an attacker generates an address that copies the first and last characters of a real one, hoping someone later copies it from a transaction history by mistake. On Jan. 28, 2025, an address beginning 18VpNbPc and ending pQ9x sent the wallet 600 sats, and it shares the first three and last four characters with the whale’s address.
The look-alike was funded in a Nov. 12, 2024 transaction that paid out to 1,401 outputs at once, and it was emptied after sending that one payment. Every other sender used a bc1 address, which looks nothing like the wallet’s legacy 18 address.
The whale hasn’t fallen for it.
Large holders of Bitcoin, known as whales, move their coins for different reasons, including privacy and safety. Analysts and traders fear that moves like that precede selling as holders feel tempted to realize significant gains.
That said, this is not the first time dormant wallets move their coins. Back in July 2025, an entity moved 80,000 BTC that had sat for 14 years, worth $8.6 billion, the biggest daily movement of coins aged 10 years or more. Ten days later a Satoshi-era wallet sent 40,009 BTC, about $4.7 billion, to Galaxy, which later said it had executed a sale worth roughly $9 billion for a Satoshi-era client.
As of Oct. 13, the original address holds 23,288 sats in leftover dust, about $19, while the five receiving addresses hold the full 4,581.94 BTC.

articles.title: BIS: Digital Cash Offers ‘Cash-like privacy’ but Bank Data Breaches Threaten Users
articles.text:
Digital cash offers ‘cash-like privacy,’ but bank data breaches threaten users: BIS
BIS said that digital cash can achieve “cash-like privacy,” however, the technology isn’t yet production-ready due to risks such as bank data breaches.
The Bank for International Settlements (BIS) said digital cash can offer privacy properties similar to cash, but highlighted remaining risks, including how potential bank data breaches may expose users’ personal data.
While digital cash can achieve “cash-like privacy,” the technology stack is not yet “production ready,” wrote BIS in its Project Aurum Phase 2 report, published on Tuesday.
This phase implements a privacy-preserving digital cash prototype using BIS’s existing Aurum codebase to take a balanced approach between complete anonymity and full transaction transparency, BIS said.
BIS found that compromising one bank may expose its customer data, but would not expose customer identities from other counterparties. A validator-level compromise alone would not be enough to expose end users, according to the report.
The BIS report explores the technical features needed to establish a privacy-preserving central bank digital currency (CBDC). CBDC critics previously raised concerns about the technology’s potential financial surveillance capabilities.
In 2023, Brazil’s central bank published the source code for its CBDC pilot, and within days, people noticed the surveillance and control mechanisms embedded within its code, allowing the central bank to freeze or reduce user funds within CBDC wallets.
Earlier this year, US President Donald Trump banned federal agencies from issuing a CBDC in January, citing financial stability and privacy concerns.
Related: Republican lawmakers call for permanent CBDC ban as House vote approaches

articles.title: Strive Buys $280 Million in Bitcoin, Its Largest Purchase in Months - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Strive bought 3,311 BTC worth roughly $280 million between Oct. 5 and Oct. 9 at an average price of about $84,500 per coin, its largest purchase since January, lifting holdings to 32,773 BTC.
- The buy caps an aggressive run—following $169 million and $94.5 million purchases—for the firm, which trades as ASST and recently merged with Semler Scientific to grow its balance sheet.
- It lands amid heavy treasury activity from Strategy, Solana’s DeFi Dev Corp. and Bitmine, as Strive bought into a dip well below Bitcoin’s recent highs.
Strive is piling into Bitcoin at its fastest clip of the year, scooping up another 3,311 BTC worth roughly $280 million in its biggest single purchase since January.
The Nasdaq-listed asset manager, which trades under the ticker ASST, disclosed in a filing Monday that it bought the Bitcoin between Oct. 5 and Oct. 9 at an average price of about $84,500 per coin, including fees. The buy lifts Strive’s total holdings to 32,773 BTC, worth roughly $2.73 billion at today’s prices, up from 29,462 BTC a week earlier.
The purchase caps a stretch of aggressive accumulation. Strive added $169 million in Bitcoin earlier this month in what was then its largest buy in four months, after pushing its stack past 27,000 BTC with a $94.5 million purchase in late September.
The latest tranche extends that momentum, and the timing is notable: the firm bought as Bitcoin slid through a rough week, picking up coins at an average price well below the token’s recent highs near $87,000.
Strive, led by CEO Matthew Cole, is among a wave of public companies that have adopted Bitcoin treasury strategies, raising capital to stockpile the asset and tie their share price to its performance.
The model, pioneered by Michael Saylor’s Strategy, has drawn a crowded field, and Strive has moved aggressively since going public through its merger with Asset Entities, recently completing a tie-up with Semler Scientific to bulk up its balance sheet. Beyond its Bitcoin, the company also holds about 505,000 shares of Strategy’s STRC preferred stock, valued near $50 million, and roughly $310 million in cash.
The buying spree arrives amid a flurry of treasury activity across the sector. Strategy itself recently added $21.5 million in Bitcoin while buying back preferred stock, Solana treasury firm DeFi Development Corp. kept accumulating SOL, and Bitmine continued stacking Ethereum, though chairman Tom Lee said that company is nearly finished and will halt purchases once it holds 5% of the token’s supply.
The strategy carries the category’s familiar risk: Strive’s fortunes rise and fall with a notoriously volatile asset. Buying into a dip can pay off if Bitcoin rebounds, but the same exposure cuts the other way, and treasury firms have faced scrutiny over how much their stock premiums depend on continued accumulation.

articles.title: Sberbank Secures Russia’s Approval for Crypto Trading
articles.text:
Russia clears Sberbank for crypto trading ahead of December launch
Russia’s largest bank, Sberbank, has secured crypto exchange authorization as it prepares to offer Bitcoin, Ether and Tether USDt trading.
Sberbank, Russia’s largest lender, has secured the central bank’s approval to trade cryptocurrencies, including Bitcoin, ahead of a planned December launch.
The Bank of Russia’s updated register, dated Tuesday, lists 10 authorized crypto exchange operators and six digital custodians, up from four and five, respectively, a week earlier. The lists include major lenders Sberbank and VTB alongside nonbank companies such as T-Invest Lab and Atomyze.
Sberbank previously said it plans to launch crypto products supporting Bitcoin (BTC), Ether (ETH) and Tether’s USDt (USDT) on Dec. 1, 2026, through its existing SberBank Online, SberInvestments and SberBusiness platforms.
Sberbank has already begun testing crypto purchases, sales, deposits and withdrawals through its SberBank Online app, Russian business newspaper Vedomosti reported on Thursday, citing the bank’s press office. The bank said the final launch timeline depends on additional central bank regulations.
The registrations follow the Sept. 1 entry into force of Russia’s new crypto rules, which placed exchange operators and custodians under central bank oversight. The country still prohibits using cryptocurrencies to pay for goods and services.
Sberbank was among the first companies to secure digital custodian status last Tuesday.
Related: UK sanctions three crypto exchanges tied to Russian illicit funds

articles.title: AI Researchers Are Smoking Cigarettes to Prove AI Will Cure Cancer, Says Palantir Exec - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Palantir CTO Shyam Sankar claimed on CBS that many AI researchers have started smoking to show how much they believe in AI.
- Sankar provide any data, and used the segment to attack effective altruism as a doomsday cult.
- The CDC says smoking causes about one in three U.S. cancer deaths, and Anthropic's Dario Amodei says only actually curing cancer will earn public trust in AI.
Nothing says "I trust the future of medicine" quite like lighting a Marlboro and waiting for the chatbot to fix your lungs. That is the habit Palantir CTO Shyam Sankar says is spreading among AI researchers, who have supposedly started smoking cigarettes to prove how confident they are that AI will cure cancer.
"So many AI researchers have started smoking as a way of signaling to other researchers how much they believe in AI," Sankar said in an interview on CBS News' "Face the Nation" on Sunday. "I believe so much in AI that it's going to cure cancer. So I'm showing you my chips are all in."
He did not name a single researcher, cite a survey, or explain how he knows. The remark landed as an aside while host Margaret Brennan pressed him on why he was so focused on the topic.
He pointed to FTX founder Sam Bankman-Fried as the effective altruist most Americans know, calling the movement a "millenarian doomsday cult." He also invoked Pascal's idea of a god-shaped hole in every human heart, which he suggested some of these researchers are filling with a machine god called AGI.
The medical record is less enthusiastic than the thesis. The CDC says smoking causes roughly one in three cancer deaths in the United States, and cigarette smoke contains at least 69 chemicals known to cause cancer.
Smokers face about 25 times the lung cancer risk of non-smokers, according to the agency. Quitting lowers the risk of 12 types of cancer, and the added lung cancer risk drops by half 10 to 15 years after stopping.
The cancer pitch is not new in this industry. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said in August that promising AI will cure cancer has become “more a cliche than it is inspiring,” and that only actually curing it would earn the public's trust.
2/2 Second, on the messaging around AI. I do not agree that my messaging has been disproportionately negative. In fact it has been about equally balanced between risks and benefits: I’ve written one major essay about each, and even in interviews where I discuss the risks, I…
— Dario Amodei (@DarioAmodei) August 15, 2026
That trust is thin. In the CBS poll Brennan cited, 50% of Americans said AI will create more problems than it solves, 29% said it will solve more than it creates, and 21% were unsure.
About 45% said they want the government to restrict AI's use and development. Smoking to show faith in the technology does not obviously help that number, but it does help AI bros bond with each other. "When you're smoking, you're networking by accident," Revamp AI cofounder Stephen Campbell told Business Insider last month.
The IMF's Kristalina Georgieva recently warned that AI could hit 40% of jobs, and insiders expect a major AI incident within a year. Indirectly causing a lung cancer outbreak was probably not on their bingo card.
Palantir sells data-analysis software to governments and militaries. Most of its business relies on AI.

articles.title: ENS Proposes Moving Ethereum Domain Registrations to Upgraded System
articles.text:
ENS seeks DAO approval to activate upgraded Ethereum naming system
New .eth registrations would pause for hours during the transition, while existing domain holders could renew their names without migrating.
Ethereum Name Service (ENS) is seeking approval from its decentralized autonomous organization (DAO) to activate an upgraded naming protocol on the Ethereum mainnet.
ENS founder Nick Johnson submitted an executable draft proposal to activate ENSv2, the next version of the protocol. If approved, the upgrade would freeze new registrations on the original ENS registrar while allowing existing domain holders to continue renewing their names.
The upgrade introduces a redesigned registry architecture with more flexible domain management and permissions. After the activation, ENS Labs plans to transfer its remaining administrative control over the upgraded contracts to the DAO.
New .eth registrations would move to the upgraded system once domain records have been synchronized. Johnson warned that new registrations would be temporarily unavailable on either version for several hours during the transition.
Existing domain holders are not required to migrate, and their names would continue functioning normally, according to the proposal. ENS Labs also reserved existing .eth names for their current owners on the upgraded system, allowing users to migrate when ready.
The activation proposal remains in draft stage and must advance to an onchain DAO vote before implementation.
Under ENS governance rules, executable proposals require at least 1% voter participation, representing 1 million ENS votes, and majority approval during a seven-day voting period. If approved, the upgrade would be subject to a minimum two-day timelock before execution. A voting date has not yet been announced.
Related: Ethereum’s zkAPI brings privacy-preserving API payments to mainnet

articles.title: Bitcoin Shakes Off Spooky Season Jitters: Can Bulls Keep It Going? - Decrypt

Traders on Myriad, a prediction market developed by Decrypt's parent company Dastan, give 54% odds that Bitcoin falls to $80,000 this month, down from 56% on Monday. The BTC highs in October market holds at 45% for $87,500. So, overall, sentiment has improved today, even if slightly.
Bitcoin price: Bulls defend the golden zone
Today's low stopped about $588 above $80,365.12, the swing low where the bounce began. That higher low is what traders want in an uptrend. Bitcoin also reclaimed the Fibonacci "golden zone" between $81,847.57 and $82,305.50, an area where pullbacks within uptrends often draw buyers.

Until Wednesday's CPI print, the active squeeze points to a market that is winding up rather than picking a direction. Oil and Iran headlines, Treasury yields, and daily ETF flows remain the short-term catalysts to track.
